facts.statement: The genus Jidapterus was named in 2003 by Dong Zhiming, Sun Yue-Wu, and Wu Shao-Yuan.
facts.quote: The genus was in 2003 named by Dong Zhiming, Sun Yue-Wu and Wu Shao-Yuan.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Jidapterus edentus.
facts.quote: The type species is Jidapterus edentus.

facts.statement: The genus name combines "Jilin University" with the Greek word for wing.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from Jílín Dàxué or "Jilin University" and a Latinized Greek pteron, "wing".

facts.statement: The specific name edentus means "toothless" in Latin.
facts.quote: The specific name means "toothless" in Latin.

facts.statement: The skull is toothless, relatively long, and features a straight, pointed beak with a large opening connecting the antorbital fenestra to the nostrils.
facts.quote: The skull is toothless and relatively long, with a straight and very pointed beak, and a large hole where the antorbital fenestra is joined with the nostrils.

facts.statement: The animal had small eye sockets, lacked a lower jaw crest found in ornithocheiroids, but possessed a short projection at the back of the skull.
facts.quote: The eye sockets are small, and there is no crest along the lower jaw as seen in ornithocheiroids, although a short projection was present at the back of the skull.

facts.statement: The estimated wingspan of the known individual is 1.7 meters.
facts.quote: The wingspan of this individual was estimated to be 1.7 m.

facts.statement: Jidapterus lived during the Aptian stage of the Lower Cretaceous in the Jiufotang Formation of Chaoyang, Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Jidapterus is a genus of chaoyangopterid pterosaur from the Aptian-age Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Chaoyang, Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: David Unwin initially placed Jidapterus in Tapejaridae but later agreed it belonged to the family Chaoyangopteridae as a close relative of Chaoyangopterus.
facts.quote: David Unwin assigned it to Tapejaridae without comment in The Pterosaurs: From Deep Time, but later, in a collaboration with Lü, agreed that it belonged to another azhdarchoid group and was a close relative of Chaoyangopterus, placing both in the new family Chaoyangopteridae.

facts.statement: A 2017 redescription confirmed the placement of Jidapterus in Chaoyangopteridae and provided evidence distinguishing it from Chaoyangopterus.
facts.quote: A redescription of the genus in 2017 corroborated these results, and also presented evidence distinguishing it from Chaoyangopterus.

facts.statement: The genus is classified within the family Chaoyangopteridae.
The Paleobiology Database lists Chaoyangopterinae as the parent group for Jidapterus.
The Paleobiology Database lists Tapejaridae as the family for Jidapterus.
The classification of Jidapterus has been unstable, with original authors failing to assign it to a specific group.
facts.quote: The classification of Jidapterus has been unstable; the original authors did not assign it to a group.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding whether Jidapterus is a basal azhdarchoid or closely related to Pteranodon and the genus Chaoyangopterus.
facts.quote: Some of the original authors later suggested it was a more basal azhdarchoid, whereas another group suggested it was closer to Pteranodon and possibly the same genus as Chaoyangopterus.

rejected.statement: The genus is known from holotype CAD-01, a nearly complete skeleton with a partial skull.
rejected.quote: Jidapterus is based on holotype CAD-01, a nearly complete skeleton with partial skull.
